html:
(a) A survey of 400 randomly selected Year 12 students found 20% of them were in favour of shorter summer holidays.

Using z=2, determine an approximate 95% confidence interval for the proportion of all Year 12s in favour of shorter summer holidays. (3 marks)

(b) In order to estimate how many people would vote for a particular political party, p, a group of randomly selected voters is surveyed. The survey resulted in a 95% symmetrical confidence interval of 0.498<p<0.522.

Below are five statements about this confidence interval. Tick the two correct statements.

(2 marks)

The probability that a randomly selected voter will vote for the party is between 0.498 and 0.522.
A 90% confidence interval determined based on the data collected would have a smaller interval width.
Assuming that the proportion of voters in the sample remains the same, increasing the sample size would lead to a reduction in the 95% confidence interval.
The probability that party A will receive a vote share of more than 52.2% is 5%.
A majority of voters would vote for this political party in an election.
